claims.text: The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy lacks a robust, self-forming protective oxide layer under extreme-temperature conditions.
Pack aluminization will enrich the alloy surface with aluminum.
Pack aluminization will improve the alloy's high-temperature oxygen resistance.
The aluminization treatment will promote formation of a dense, adherent Al2O3 surface layer.
At high temperature, the aluminum-enriched surface will react with oxygen to form a continuous alumina scale.
The continuous alumina scale will act as a diffusion barrier.
The alumina diffusion barrier will reduce oxygen ingress into the alloy.
Reduced oxygen ingress will decrease the oxidation rate relative to the untreated alloy.
After approximately 100 hours at 1000°C in air, the aluminized alloy will have lower oxidation weight gain than the untreated alloy.
After approximately 100 hours at 1000°C in air, the aluminized alloy will exhibit minimal oxide-scale growth.
The aluminized alloy will oxidize at less than half the rate of the untreated alloy under the stated conditions.
The untreated alloy will develop a less protective, rapidly growing oxide layer at 1000°C in air for 100 hours.
The untreated alloy will undergo greater overall oxidation than the aluminized alloy under the stated conditions.
Analogous studies on aluminized alloys support the proposed mechanism.
The effectiveness of aluminization may differ at significantly higher temperatures or in different oxidizing environments.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies an oxidation rate below half that of the untreated alloy, but the falsification rule only requires a statistically significant reduction. A significant reduction smaller than 50% would fail the quantitative prediction without satisfying the stated falsification condition.
